# Checking a request against existing tickets

Follow this before a ticket is created on the change and queue routes. The creating command compares the request with the tickets of every status, done and dropped included, and prints the likeliest matches; you judge them, and the owner decides on a real match.

1. Turn the request into a short title in English, in business language, keeping the owner's meaning. The owner may chat in another language and tickets are English; the owner may change the title before the ticket is created.
2. Run the creating command with `--title "<title>"`. It prints up to five `similar: <id> "<title>" (<status>)` lines, or `similar: none`. With `similar: none` it has created the ticket: go on. With candidates it exits 2 and writes nothing.
3. Read each candidate's title and status, open its ticket file when the title is not enough, and judge which really match the request: the same outcome wanted, not only shared words.
4. On a match, ask the owner one question as `./ask.md` says, with three options and what each does:
   - continue the existing ticket: `/accord-continue <id>`, or `/accord-pickup <id>` for a ticket nobody has claimed;
   - merge this request into it: add the request to that ticket as the existing-ticket route of `/accord` says;
   - create a new ticket linked to it: run the creating command again with `--related <id>`.
5. On no match, run the creating command again with `--related none` and ask the owner nothing.

No scout runs for this check: it reads tickets, and the scout reads code.
